catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-cite: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Cîteaux — the mother-house of the Cistercian Order — tells of Robert of Molesme's reform. Marie Gildas recounts its austere beginnings. An essential reference on monastic renewal. White habits and strict silence began in its Burgundian fields.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-clai: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Clairvaux — St. Bernard's great foundation — traces its rise to European influence. Marie Gildas celebrates the mellifluous doctor's home. A central reference on the Cistercians. Bernard's letters flew from Clairvaux to popes and kings.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arnulf-of-lis: A 1913 entry on Arnulf of Lisieux — the bishop and statesman. Thomas Shahan honors his letters. He served Henry II's troubled reign. The schools prized his Latin. A prelate of the Angevin court. His see guarded the Norman coast. His letters survive in the collections.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bayeux: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Bayeux — the Norman diocese of the tapestry town. Georges Goyau gives its story. Its cathedral crowns the old streets. The embroidery tells the Conquest's tale. A see of the Calvados. Its lace is famed through France.
